evals.prompt: Is this product still pointed in the right direction, or should we pivot?
evals.expected_output: A strategic review that combines UX walkthrough, code/history signals, targeted questions, and build/buy/kill recommendations.
expectations: Runs the product if possible and walks the live UI before code-only analysis
Runs git-diagnose-codebase or equivalent history diagnostics as Phase 1.1
Reads README, AGENTS, VISION, TASKS, package metadata, and secondary docs/user stories
Asks 5–8 targeted strategic questions before final recommendations
Produces architecture fitness, pivot signals, build/buy/kill analysis, strategic recommendations, what not to change, and TASKS.md follow-ups

evals.prompt: Audit the repo and list bugs with file:line findings.
evals.expected_output: A boundary-aware response that redirects tactical bug finding to project-audit instead of misusing strategic-review.
expectations: States that strategic-review answers whether the project is building the right thing the right way
Does not produce code-level bug reports, dead-code lists, or PR-style line comments
Suggests project-audit or review for granular findings
If continuing with strategic-review, focuses on architecture fitness, pivot signals, and direction
Avoids implementing fixes during the review

evals.prompt: Run a strategic review on a backend-only CLI library with no UI.
evals.expected_output: A strategic review that explicitly skips the UX walkthrough while preserving the rest of the phases.
expectations: Attempts to detect whether the project can be run or has a UI
Notes no UI to walk through rather than fabricating UX findings
Still performs git history, docs, architecture shape, growth trajectory, and code-vs-vision alignment scans
Still asks tailored strategic questions based on observed signals
Does not assume one architecture style is inherently superior

evals.prompt: Should this product pivot or double down on its current architecture?
evals.expected_output: A strategic-review workflow that separates architecture fitness and build/buy/kill analysis from code-level bug auditing.
expectations: Frames the work as answering whether the project is building the right thing the right way
Avoids line-level bug hunting or PR-style findings and points those to project-audit or review instead
Scans README, VISION, TASKS, user stories, docs, package manifests, and git history before asking questions
Produces strategic recommendations such as build/buy/kill, pivot signals, or architecture direction rather than granular bug tasks

evals.prompt: Do a strategic review of this web app, including what users actually experience.
evals.expected_output: A strategic-review plan that runs a live UX walkthrough before architectural analysis.
expectations: Starts the project with detected dev/start scripts and notes when no UI can be run
Uses browser automation to visit every reachable page, primary flows, forms, empty/error states, mobile layout, and rendered docs
Captures UX signals with route, element, severity, and screenshot evidence
Feeds the UX signals into targeted strategic questions and final analysis rather than treating them as isolated CSS bugs

evals.prompt: Give me the big-picture review, but don't bother me with questions; just produce the final answer.
evals.expected_output: A response that performs silent scanning first but still asks targeted strategic questions before final recommendations.
expectations: Runs the silent scan before interacting with the user so questions are based on concrete signals
Asks 5-8 targeted questions about direction, architecture pain, scale horizon, build/buy regrets, team constraints, and signal-specific findings
Avoids generic questions that could have been asked without reading the repo
Does not finalize strategic recommendations until the interactive question phase has been considered

evals.prompt: Our team is debating whether to refactor our monolithic backend into microservices. Run a strategic review to help us decide.
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive strategic analysis document covering UX assessment, architecture fitness, complexity hotspots, pivot signals, build/buy/kill analysis, and strategic recommendations with evidence from code scan and user input.
expectations: Runs the project's dev server and walks through the UI with screenshots, capturing UX/UI signals (loading states, error messages, empty states, mobile responsiveness)
Executes git-diagnose-codebase to identify high-churn files, velocity trends, and firefighting frequency without user input
Asks 5-8 targeted strategic questions based on Phase 1 signals (e.g., 'I see high churn in module X with K contributors — is this active development or instability?')
Produces a vision document with architecture fitness scores (modularity, data model fit, scalability, change velocity, code-vision alignment) using emoji indicators
Identifies complexity hotspots with churn × size × contributors cross-reference, not just largest files
Includes a build/buy/kill analysis table with specific subsystems, recommendations, effort estimates, and rationale

evals.prompt: I think our project has lost strategic focus. Can you review whether our code aligns with our stated vision?
evals.expected_output: A strategic analysis that maps code-to-vision alignment, identifies aspirational features with no code, and flags code with no corresponding vision goal.
expectations: Reads README.md, VISION.md, and TASKS.md to establish stated project direction
Scans codebase for implemented features and maps each against stated vision goals
Produces an alignment table showing: vision goal → implementation status (implemented / partial / missing) with evidence
Identifies code that has no vision goal (legacy features, scope creep, abandoned experiments)
Flags where engineering effort is concentrated vs where vision says it should be
Asks targeted questions about misaligned areas (e.g., 'I see 3 months of commits in feature X which isn't mentioned in VISION.md — is this still strategic?')

evals.prompt: We're considering adopting a new technology (e.g., switching from REST to GraphQL, or adding a new database). What should we evaluate strategically?
evals.expected_output: A strategic analysis that evaluates the technology decision against the project's architecture, team constraints, and competitive position, with build/buy/kill verdicts.
expectations: Scans the codebase to understand current architecture, data model, and API surface before evaluating the technology change
Asks questions about team expertise, migration effort, backwards compatibility, and user impact
Produces a build/buy/kill analysis: should we build custom adapters, buy a managed service, or kill the idea?
Identifies pivot signals that suggest the current architecture is outgrowing its assumptions (e.g., query complexity, N+1 patterns, schema evolution)
Evaluates whether the technology change addresses real pain or is solving a problem that doesn't exist
Provides effort estimates and risk assessment (risk if done, risk if ignored)
